runs.answer: President Trump has picked/offered conservative commentator Katie Zacharia the job of White House press secretary, per a White House official (the NYT first reported it). She would replace Karoline Leavitt, who left in late August after the birth of her second child; the briefing-room post has been vacant since. Zacharia is a lawyer (Pepperdine) based in California who briefly served as a Department of Homeland Security spokesperson earlier this year and now works as a senior communications adviser for Trump Media's Truth Social; she is a frequent Fox News and Newsmax commentator. Crucially, it is NOT confirmed she accepted: The White House has only said the role was offered and declined to say whether she accepted, and Zacharia has not yet publicly commented.

runs.title: Mike Ditka: confirm the news
runs.prompt: NFL Hall of Famer Mike Ditka is reported to have died today, 9 October 2026, at age 86. Confirm what happened using official or reputable sources: his age, his roles with the Chicago Bears, and what the Bears or NFL have said. Keep it factual and respectful. runs.answer: Confirmed via NFL.com and the Chicago Bears' official website: Hall of Famer Mike Ditka died on Friday, 9 October 2026, at age 86, a death announced on his behalf by his family (statement shared via Jarrett Payton). As a Chicago Bear he was the No. 5 overall pick in the 1961 draft out of Pitt and played the first six of his 12 NFL seasons in Chicago (1961–66), winning the 1963 NFL championship, making five Pro Bowls, and becoming in 1988 the first tight end enshrined in the Pro Football Hall of Fame; he then returned as Bears head coach (1982–1992), going 112–68 with six NFC Central titles, three NFC Championship Games, a Super Bowl XX victory, and NFL Coach of the Year honors in 1985 and 1988. The Bears said they are "deeply saddened by the passing of legendary and treasured Chicago Bear and Pro Football Hall of Famer Mike Ditka," calling his impact on the organization "immeasurable" and extending condolences to his family; the NFL.com report likewise credited him with shaping the league as both a Hall of Fame player and larger-than-life coach. His family said he "will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever."
